setup: Both APIs searched the **same OpenSearch index** (PaperPilot's, port 9210): the Python API ran with `OPENSEARCH_HOST` pointed at it, so the data was identical without re-seeding.
Both used the host's Ollama with `qwen3.5:9b` and thinking off. The stacks ran one after the other, never at the same time, so neither competed with the other for the GPU.
The Python API ran with Langfuse and Telegram off (`LANGFUSE__ENABLED=false`, `TELEGRAM__ENABLED=false`); PaperPilot ran with Langfuse on and the Telegram bot running.
Every `/ask` question is asked twice: the first call is a cache miss (none of the questions had been asked before), the second a hit.

PaperPilot was recorded after the `localhost` fix (commit 5a1c0e4). An earlier run, before it, had a cache-miss p50 of 40.7 s. Ollama generated at the same rate for both stacks (about 7.3 tokens/s), so cache-miss latency follows answer length, which varies from run to run (sampling settings differ, B29; chat API instead of one prompt, C3). Three of its requests had also spent 2 s connecting to `localhost` over IPv6 before falling back to IPv4.

PaperPilot's times for g10–g20 are too slow: a second PaperPilot run, started by mistake, was generating `/ask` answers on the same GPU at the time. Asked again on their own afterwards, g11–g20 took 4.7–7.1 s each (Python: 5.9–8.2 s). Agentic latency isn't one of the checks, and the guardrail decisions and sources don't depend on speed.

explanations.agentic.sources: B1: Python's `/ask-agentic` never fills `sources` (`relevant_sources` is never set, and `_extract_sources` returns dicts for a `List[str]` field), so every answer comes back with `[]`. PaperPilot lists the PDFs of the chunks the answer was generated from.
